tshelter.msg.111: Life support and climate control system.
tshelter.msg.201: System check - All system components are operating normally. A comprehensive environmental analysis (including air and soil samples) carried out by the sensors on the surface has shown conditions to be satisfactory and safe for human presence on the surface. Accordingly, the system has decided to reduce power consumption by shutting down the "sealed climate" mode, along with those units not required for standard operation.
tshelter.msg.202: [After a short wait, a yellow smiley face assembles itself out of pixels, periodically sticking out its tongue, along with a scrolling line: "Foxx Enterteinment & Co.". Nothing else happens.]
tshelter.msg.203:
Project "FRs". "Version 1" - Released under public pressure. Prototype non-functional. "Version 2" - Test. Functionality questionable. "Version 3" - No data. "Version 4" - Stable operation. Contains critical errors. "Version 5" - Stable operation. Corrections underway. "Version 6" - Working model. Stabilization, added functionality. Handed over to another department. "Version 7" - Working model. No data.                                                            
Project leader: Pyran. Technical staff: ViKey, Mr.Fakelman.
tshelter.msg.204: <...> Myself, Jane Valentine, Pacman* and Premier*. We managed to obtain the archives, but they turned out to be useless, we didn't understand how to read them. Through trial and error, the principle of reading the archives' cipher became clear to us. The work took off. Jane cracked them in no time, but one day she simply vanished. Premier disappeared next. The last thing he said was: - something urgent has come up. We never saw them again... Some time later, several people joined us. Though not everything went so smoothly. Some turned out to be scoundrels who caused no end of trouble. We had to deal with them personally. It's a good thing that Doctor Victor was with us during that period, with him around we no longer worried much about chancers of any kind.
tshelter.msg.205: Time passed, the archives grew fewer, as did the like-minded... <...> there were two of us left - myself and Pacman. I began going up to the surface more often, Pacman carried on studying the archives, throwing himself into the work completely. <...> a great deal of work was done, but we did it.
